headline: Scientists Unlock New Way to Protect Cells' Energy Factories
meta_description: Researchers at Politecnico di Milano have developed a technique to coat mitochondria with advanced materials while preserving their energy-producing function,…
summary_short: A breakthrough coating technique could transform treatment of mitochondrial diseases. Scientists preserved the energy-making ability of these cellular powerhouses using…
body:
Researchers at Politecnico di Milano and the Fondazione Istituto Neurologico Carlo Besta have achieved something previously thought risky: coating mitochondria—the tiny structures that generate energy inside our cells—with advanced materials without damaging their function. The discovery, published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society, represents a significant step toward treating diseases caused by malfunctioning mitochondria, conditions that disproportionately affect energy-hungry tissues like the brain and muscles. The team, led by Dr. Valeria Tiranti and Professor Pierangelo Metrangolo through their joint BraiNs laboratory established in 2023, used Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOF)—materials whose properties can be customized for specific purposes—to create the protective coating.

The challenge was formidable: mitochondria are extraordinarily delicate structures that easily lose their ability to function if disturbed. The researchers overcame this by applying tiny amounts of MOF directly to the mitochondrial surface in a way that allowed these cellular powerhouses to continue producing energy without interruption. Tests confirmed the coated mitochondria maintained their essential function, opening entirely new research directions.

Perhaps most exciting is the potential for mitochondrial transplantation—an experimental technique where healthy mitochondria could be introduced into cells with damaged ones. A specially engineered coating might eventually facilitate this transfer and help transplanted mitochondria interact successfully with recipient cells. However, researchers emphasize this possibility remains unproven and requires further investigation. What's clear is that this work, funded through Italy's Health Operational Plan, demonstrates how combining mitochondrial biology expertise with advanced materials chemistry can yield breakthroughs that might one day transform treatment options for patients with rare mitochondrial diseases.
quick_facts: Politecnico di Milano and Fondazione Istituto Neurologico Carlo Besta partnered on the breakthrough
Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOF) applied without disrupting mitochondrial energy production
BraiNs laboratory joint collaboration established in 2023
Findings published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society in October 2026
Potential future application: transplanting healthy mitochondria into damaged cells
